name: AML compliance pack for small jewellers and precious-metal buyers (UIF Res. 54/2024 and 55/2024)
buyer: Small jewellers, gold buyers and precious-metal traders (sujetos obligados)
trigger: UIF Res. 54/2024 and 55/2024 (March 2024) replaced Res. 28/2011; national; obligations for the whole production chain, registration and reporting.
existing: Generic AML/UIF compliance software exists (unchecked); likely a generic category. Competitor search not run (budget).
unchecked: Size thresholds and reporting frequency of Res. 54/55; number of small jewellers actually in scope; the 2025 Boletín Oficial notice; local competitors.

first_check.duty: UIF Res. 55/2024 (in force since 26/03/2024), under Ley 25.246 art. 20 inc. 16. Clients are defined at 6 or more SMVM. The monthly RSM covers operations over 20 SMVM and is filed between days 1 and 15; a "sin movimientos" report is required in months with nothing to report. The annual RSA is filed between 2 Jan and 15 Mar. The ITAER risk self-assessment and the risk tolerance declaration are due every two years by 30 April (first deadline 30/04/2026, covering 2024 and 2025). Legal persons need a compliance officer and an internal audit. An independent external review is required above 180 SMVM a year (first report due by 31/10/2026). Sanctions follow Ley 25.246 Ch. IV. Res. 54/2024 covers art, antiques and numismatics, not jewellery. Registration in SRO+ was fully digitalised by Res. 37/2026. I could not open the 2025 Boletín Oficial notice (aviso 305168, 503 error), so it is not_reached.
first_check.market: Unverified. I found no UIF statistic on how many inc. 16 entities are registered, and the UIF 2024 management summary PDF could not be parsed. The scope is broad (mining, gold buyers, refiners, manufacturers, artisans, retailers), but how many are actually registered and above the thresholds is unknown, and enforcement against small informal gold buyers is likely weak.
first_check.competitor: Reports are filed on UIF's free SRO+ portal, which handles submission but not record-keeping, risk scoring or the self-assessment. Three Spanish-language searches for Argentine AML software (jewellers, DNFBPs, RSM/legajo) found no jeweller-specific product. The only jeweller-specific AML tool that came up, kyc-systems.com, is Mexican (LFPIORPI). Accountants and AML consultants offer generic services, and the professional councils (consejo.org.ar, FACPCE) publish self-assessment guides for their own members. Regional or generic AML vendors were not checked exhaustively.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. UIF Res. 55/2024 (BO 26/03/2024, which replaced Res. 28/2011) covers the whole jewellery and precious-metal chain down to retailers and artisans. It requires a monthly RSM report (days 1-15, operations over 20 SMVM, or a "sin movimientos" filing when there are none), an annual RSA (2 Jan-15 Mar) and a two-yearly risk self-assessment due by 30 April (first one in 2026). It also requires a compliance officer and an internal audit, plus an external review above 180 SMVM a year. Penalties follow Ley 25.246 Ch. IV. Filing itself goes through UIF's free SRO+ portal. I found no jeweller-specific Argentine AML software. Downsides: I found no figure for how many firms are in scope, many small jewellers are informal, willingness to pay is likely low, and accountants already sell this as a service.

challenge_check.killer: None found. There is no Argentine jeweller-specific AML product, no free UIF tool beyond the filing portal, and no exemption for small firms.
challenge_check.reason: The duty is real and recurring. Res. 55/2024 covers the whole jewellery and precious-metal chain with no size exemption. It requires a monthly RSM for operations above 20 SMVM, an annual RSA, a compliance officer, an annual manual review, annual training records, and a two-yearly self-assessment (first due 30 Apr 2026). Firms above 180 SMVM a year also need an external review (first due 31 Oct 2026); smaller legal persons need an internal audit. Five searches found no Argentine AML software for these firms, only law and consulting firms. Risks: the market size is unknown, past enforcement was weak (2014: fines of AR$221.7M imposed, about AR$250k collected), and thresholds may be revised. Accountants pressed UIF in 2026 for extensions and new thresholds, and UIF already moved accountants' external review to March 2027.
